mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in FEDFUNDS above 5% over two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 5% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in GDPC1 of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives lower equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% YoY.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in UNRATE above 6.5% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained high unemployment rates (>6.5%).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in INDPRO of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals weakening industrial production, which reduces corporate revenue prospects and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < previous month and < previous month - 0.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when INDPRO declines by more than 0.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent monthly decline in both GDPC1 and HOUST signals deteriorating housing and overall demand, which reduces consumer spending and capital expenditures, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both decline month-over-month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both GDPC1 and HOUST decline month-over-month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 5-year averages signals a monetary policy tightening coinciding with rising inflation, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 5-year averages.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in PAYEMS above its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS is above its 12-month moving average for four months.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in RSAFS above its 12-month average for six consecutive months signals rising household savings, which may reflect precautionary behavior and reduced consumption, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month average for six consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when RSAFS is above its 12-month average for six months.
